title: Tenant-aware gradual hotswap: automated private data-plane upgrades with safepoints and fast rollback
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Implement an automated, tenant-aware upgrade flow for Private (VPC) data planes that performs a hotswap-style component upgrade with zero-minute customer-visible downtime for steady-state traffic and deterministic fast rollback to a safepoint if regressions are detected. The flow must be driven by Terraform/IaC modules and the Private operator, include health gating based on per-tenant KPIs and SLOs, support operator-initiated emergency revert, and produce comprehensive telemetry and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: A Terraform module exists to create and manage per-tenant upgrade blueprints (canary group definitions, safepoint markers, mirror targets)
Upgrade operator implements staged hotswap steps: prepare, mirror, promote, finalize, with idempotency and retry semantics
Health gating: per-tenant latency P95, error-rate, and KV-consistency checks evaluated at each stage; thresholds are configurable via IaC
Automatic rollback to last safepoint when any gating threshold is breached, with telemetried reason logged and Slack/pager notification
Upgrade run produces a artifacts bundle: plan.json (Terraform plan), rollout-log (line-delimited events), and a post-mortem template if rollback triggered
E2E test harness simulates noisy tenants, stateful KV traffic, and validates zero-request-loss for non-affected tenants
Runbook is written, reviewed by SRE and Security, and linked from Console upgrade dashboard
tasks: Design IaC schema for per-tenant upgrade manifests and safepoint markers
Implement Terraform module private_upgrade.blueprint with inputs: tenant_id, canary_fraction, mirror_ratio, safepoint_ttl
Add per-node health-check hook that verifies KV prefix reconciliation and kernel/quantization variant compatibility
Wire SLO-gating service: subscribe to metrics, evaluate thresholds, emit discrete gating events to operator
Integrate with Console to display live rollout state, per-tenant metrics and provide manual abort/promote buttons
Author runbooks (operator manual, emergency revert, post-rollback diagnostics)
Create E2E test scenarios and load profiles, automate in CI with simulated network partitions and node restarts
Create GitHub PR template that links Terraform plan and operator e2e output; require security-review label
design_notes: We avoid a naive draining-based rollout (node-by-node evaporative drain) because tenants may have long-lived KV sessions and session affinity. Instead, the hotswap will create a promoted parallel runtime instancegroup for the tenant subset (canaries) with mirrored traffic for a configurable window. After KV reconciliation and success criteria, we atomically flip routing for the promoted group and scale down the old group. Safepoints are captured by exporting KV checkpoint manifests and snapshotting runtime config; these are short-lived and should be garbage-collected per safepoint_ttl.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV state divergence during mirror window can surface subtle corruption. Mitigation: strict checksum reconciliation, prefix-level replay logs, and a canary that performs deterministic reads/writes to exercise hot paths

Risk: Terraform drift between operator-managed computed resources and IaC-managed resources. Mitigation: define clear ownership boundaries in module (operator-managed = runtime pools; IaC-managed = blueprint + constraints) and add preflight drift-detection in plan stage
Risk: Elevated cost due to mirrored capacity. Mitigation: limit mirror_ratio and auto-scale down old pool immediately after promote; provide cost-estimate in plan.json
Risk: Slow rollback if safepoint snapshots are large. Mitigation: incremental safepoints (deltas) and quick-promote of last known-good group using snapshot references rather than full copy
implementation_decisions: Use an explicit 'safepoint' concept stored in object-store (encrypted) rather than depending on runtime ephemeral snapshots to allow cross-node restores
Operator will perform control-plane-only changes; data-plane snapshot/restore is delegated to a small runtime helper service to avoid bloat in operator code
Terraform modules will include a 'dry-run' mode that outputs estimated mirror cost and resource tags to be consumed by billing and owner approvals
Gating thresholds default to conservative values (latency P95 +30% over baseline, error-rate +0.5% absolute) but are configurable per tenant in blueprint
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-tenant rollout dashboard widget with P50/P95/P99 latency, 5xx rate, ingestion jitter, KV-consistency pass rate
Gating event stream exported to observability (traces and logs) with rollout_id and tenant_id tags
Pager rule: immediate when gating evaluation fails after >=2 consecutive measurement windows; otherwise page SRE if rollback triggered
Audit log entry for every promote/revert with operator identity, terraform-plan commit SHA, and snapshot id
test_plan: E2E will run three scenarios in CI: 1) small canary (5%) with benign traffic to validate runtime compatibility; 2) heavy-stateful KV workload with simulated network partition to validate reconciliation and safepoint restore; 3) noisy multi-tenant mix to validate isolation and zero-impact on unaffected tenants. Each scenario must pass a synthetic user-journey (login->generate->persist->read) with 99.9% success during the mirror window. We will also run randomized chaos jobs to kill worker pods during mirror and promote steps.
rollback_plan: Automatic: operator monitors gating stream and when a threshold breaches, it triggers revert to the latest safepoint and promotes the last-good group. Manual: 'Abort and revert' button in Console triggers same path and notifies SRE. On revert, runbook must be followed: 1) preserve current logs/snapshots, 2) escalate if revert fails after 3 attempts, 3) open incident and link to post-mortem template. Rollbacks must be idempotent and annotated in audit logs with reason and user/automation identity.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Ava Thompson: Initial design sketch posted. Decided to prefer hotswap over node drain to reduce tenant-affinity issues.
2025-02-21 - SRE Review (Maya Singh): Requested tighter gating for KV-consistency and an explicit chaos test for restart during snapshot upload.
2025-02-25 - Security Review (Diego Ramos): Approved storage encryption for safepoints; flagged KMS key rotation requirement in the runbook.

2025-03-01 - Engineering (Liam Patel): Prototype private_upgrade.blueprint Terraform module merged in feature branch; CI e2e flakiness observed under high concurrency, investigating backpressure handling
